newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE euroyen steady, key call rate up in Tokyo.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE euroyen steady, key call rate up in Tokyo.

text.p: The key March three-month Euroyen futures contract on the TIFFE was steady in late morning trading on Wednesday with few traders wanting to make new positions due to a dearth of fresh factors.

The key overnight call rate was up at 0.53-0.54 percent, compared with Tuesday's weighted average of 0.51 percent, in response to traders' disappointment over the Bank of Japan's (BOJ) neutral stance.
The BOJ fully offset a projected surplus by providing 200 billion yen to the market. Some traders had expected a fund injection of up to 300 billion yen by the central bank.
BOJ Governor Yasuo Matsushita is scheduled to hold a news conference from 0600 GMT.
But, traders said that they expect few surprises from the Governor's speech.

"They (BOJ) might want to re-run the previous speech by Matsushita taped several months ago, because there has been no basic change in his statements in the past several months," said a senior money trader at a local bank.
The BOJ, though optimistic about the near-term outlook of the economy, appears to be less confident about the long-term economic prospect, traders said.
The March was at 98.96 at 0222 GMT, unchanged from Tuesday. It opened at the morning low of 98.96.

At the outset, euroyen prices were pressured by a recovery in Japan's stock market led by the financial sector following Tuesday's news that the Long-Term Credit Bank of Japan Ltd and Swiss Bank Corp would form a strategic alliance, traders said.
The news meant Japan's ailing banking sector has been relieved of one negative factor, they added.
